pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection uses PSI Services LLC for the Occupational Licensing Electrical Trades examination program. The Connecticut E-2 Unlimited Electrical Journeyperson exam includes 80 questions, requires a 70% passing score, and allows 3.5 hours of testing time. The E-2 exam content outline includes general electrical knowledge, service, feeders, branch circuits, grounding and bonding, conductors and cables, raceways and boxes, special occupancies and equipment, electrical power, motors, low voltage, lighting, illuminated signs, fire detection and alarm systems, safety information, overcurrent protection, high voltage, and photovoltaics. Because the exam covers a wide range of topics, candidates should avoid studying only one area of the trade. A complete plan should include code navigation, theory review, calculation practice, safety knowledge, and exam-question practice. The exam may include questions based on listed reference material, trade knowledge, and general industry practices.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Candidates may use a silent, nonprinting, non-programmable calculator in the examination center. For code questions, the exam is based on the specific code edition listed by the exam provider for the scheduled examination, so candidates should pay close attention to the edition required for their exam appointment. This Ultimate Combo supports preparation with materials based on the 2026 National Electrical Code. Candidates studying for a Connecticut exam should use their study time to strengthen code-navigation habits, improve calculation speed, and review the E-2 subject areas in a balanced way.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Connecticut E-2 Unlimited Electrical Journeyperson exam is an open book examination. Candidates are responsible for bringing approved reference materials to the examination center. Reference materials may be highlighted, underlined, annotated, and indexed before the exam session. References may not be written in during the examination session. Permanent tabs and indexes are allowed when they are part of the approved reference setup. Temporary tabs, such as Post-it notes, are not allowed and must be removed before the exam begins. Candidates are not permitted to bring additional papers, loose notes, attached notes, or unapproved materials with their references. Writing questions and answers in reference materials is strictly prohibited. This makes preparation with a tabbed NEC especially valuable.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is useful for building familiarity with code layout, article structure, tables, definitions, wiring methods, grounding and bonding rules, service requirements, overcurrent protection rules, motor provisions, photovoltaic provisions, and other NEC areas that may appear in journeyperson preparation. Open book does not mean easy. Candidates still need to know where to look, how to interpret code language, and how to apply the correct rule to the question. The best study approach is to practice identifying the subject of each question first, then locating the relevant code article, table, or rule efficiently.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Connecticut electrical licensing is handled through the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection. Candidates pursuing the E-2 Unlimited Electrical Journeyperson license should follow the state application process, document required training and experience, complete the exam process through PSI, and submit any required licensing materials and fees. A typical path for an E-2 journeyperson applicant includes completing a registered apprenticeship program or qualifying through equivalent experience and training, gathering proof of classroom and on-the-job training hours, submitting the proper application materials to the Department of Consumer Protection, scheduling and taking the PSI electrical journeyperson examination, and completing licensing steps after receiving a passing score. Application Service is included with this Ultimate Combo. This support helps candidates organize the application side of the licensing process, which can be just as important as exam preparation.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Proper documentation matters because the licensing authority must review whether the candidate meets the requirements for the license type being pursued. Candidates should keep clear records of apprenticeship completion, classroom instruction, on-the-job training, employer information, license type, and any equivalent experience being used for qualification. Incomplete records can delay the licensing process, so organizing documents early is a smart part of exam preparation.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: The Connecticut E-2 Unlimited Electrical Journeyperson license allows the holder to perform electrical work as defined by Connecticut law while employed by a properly licensed contractor. To qualify for the E-2 examination, candidates must complete a registered apprenticeship program or have at least four years of equivalent experience and training. Connecticut’s E-2 pathway commonly involves 8,000 hours of on-the-job training and 720 classroom hours. Applicants using equivalent experience and training must be prepared to document that their background meets the license requirements for the category they are applying for. Connecticut uses a license classification system for electrical work. The E-1 license is the unlimited electrical contractor license, while the E-2 license is the unlimited electrical journeyperson license. Limited electrical categories also exist for specialized work, but this product is written for the Connecticut journeyperson electrician path associated with the E-2 Unlimited Electrical Journeyperson examination.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Passing the examination is one part of the licensing process. Candidates must still meet Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection requirements, submit required documents, and complete the state licensing process. Exam preparation should be paired with careful attention to application requirements, experience records, and the specific license classification being pursued.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Connecticut electrical licensing is handled through the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection. Electricians must be licensed by the Department of Consumer Protection in order to perform electrical work in the state. Connecticut licenses individuals rather than electrical companies. The state uses limited and unlimited electrical license categories, with odd-numbered licenses generally identifying contractor classifications and even-numbered licenses generally identifying journeyperson or employee classifications. The Connecticut E-1 Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination is administered by PSI. The E-1 trade exam includes 100 questions, requires a 70% passing score, and allows 4 hours of testing time. Candidates taking contractor-level exams must also pass the Business and Law examination required for contractor and dealer technician licenses. The Business and Law exam includes 50 questions, requires a 70% passing score, and allows 2 hours of testing time.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Connecticut E-1 Unlimited Electrical Contractor content outline includes General Electrical Knowledge, Service, Feeders, and Branch Circuits, Grounding and Bonding, Conductors and Cables, Raceways and Boxes, Special Occupancies and Equipment, Electrical Power, Motors, Low Voltage, Lighting, Illuminated Signs, Fire Detection and Alarm Systems, Safety Information, Overcurrent Protection, High Voltage, and Photovoltaics. The examination may also contain questions based on trade knowledge or general industry practices. PSI score reporting is provided immediately after the examination. Candidates receive an on-screen result after completing the exam. Candidates who do not pass receive diagnostic information by examination type so they can review weaker areas before retesting. Candidates should follow PSI scheduling instructions and Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection licensing instructions throughout the application and exam process.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Connecticut E-1 Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination is an open-book exam. The PSI bulletin identifies the approved reference materials allowed in the examination center and states that candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved references. Candidates may use a silent, nonprinting, non-programmable calculator in the examination center. Open book does not mean the exam is simple. Candidates still need to know how to locate information quickly, understand code structure, read questions carefully, and apply the correct rule or calculation method. A candidate who has not practiced using reference materials can lose time searching, misread exceptions, or choose answers based on memory instead of code language. Connecticut’s PSI rules allow reference materials to be highlighted, underlined, annotated, and indexed before the examination session. References may not be written in during the examination session. Candidates are not permitted to bring additional loose or attached papers with approved references.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: References may be tabbed or indexed with permanent tabs only. Temporary tabs, such as Post-it notes, are not allowed and must be removed before the exam begins. Writing questions and answers in reference materials is prohibited. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs included in this Ultimate Combo helps candidates build NEC familiarity before test day. Studying with a tabbed code book helps candidates practice moving through articles, definitions, tables, wiring methods, grounding and bonding sections, service rules, feeder requirements, branch circuit provisions, and calculation references. The goal is to become comfortable enough with the code book that reference navigation becomes part of the study routine rather than a last-minute obstacle.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Connecticut E-1 Unlimited Electrical Contractor candidates must follow the licensing process established by the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection. Candidates should first confirm the correct license classification, then complete the required experience and training documentation, apply through the Department of Consumer Protection, obtain exam eligibility, schedule the required PSI examinations, pass the trade exam and the Business and Law exam, and submit the required licensing materials after passing. For the E-1 license path, Connecticut identifies 720 classroom hours and 12,000 total hours of on-the-job training as the equivalent experience and training requirement. The listed E-1 training structure includes 8,000 apprentice on-the-job training hours plus 2 years, or 4,000 hours, of licensed on-the-job training. Classroom hours must be equivalent to the required courses for the electrical license type. On-the-job training and work experience are not accepted in place of the classroom-hour requirement.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Connecticut’s electrical licensing rules also identify the E-1 qualification standard as two years as an unlimited licensed journeyperson or at least six years of equivalent experience and training. Candidates relying on equivalent experience and training should be prepared to submit documentation such as transcripts, degrees, diplomas, out-of-state completion documentation when applicable, and notarized employer letters describing dates of employment and detailed work experience. After passing the required examination, candidates submit the licensing fee indicated on the passing score report with all passing score reports to the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection. Candidates should keep copies of application materials, score reports, training documentation, and correspondence for their records.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Connecticut requires electricians to be licensed by the Department of Consumer Protection in order to perform electrical work. The Department of Consumer Protection licenses individuals, and the state recognizes both limited and unlimited license categories. Contractor licenses generally use odd numbers, such as E-1, while journeyperson or employee licenses generally use even numbers, such as E-2. The E-1 Unlimited Electrical Contractor license is the broad unlimited contractor-level electrical license in Connecticut. The holder of the E-1 license is permitted to perform all electrical work as defined under Connecticut electrical licensing rules. The E-2 Unlimited Electrical Journeyperson license also permits broad electrical work, but only while the license holder is employed by a properly licensed contractor. Only contractors can obtain permits and sign contracts in Connecticut. Journeypersons and apprentices cannot work directly for consumers unless employed by, or employing, a licensed contractor of record.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Candidates planning to operate independently should understand the difference between contractor-level authority and journeyperson-level work authorization before selecting a license path. Connecticut also has limited electrical license categories for specific scopes of work, including line work, low voltage work, sign work, telecommunications-related work, and solar electric work. Candidates should apply for the license classification that matches the actual scope of work they intend to perform.
